generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Ranunculales page, Papaveraceae (read 2026-10-16): Papaveroideae with 4 large petals (bowl-like, inferred); Fumarioideae (more species) with spurred outer petals forming a narrow tube. 'usually' cupped reflects likely candidates; genus values needed for Fumarioideae.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, 290: stamens usually many, sometimes 4 to 6 (Fumarioideae). Book writes ∞ (numerous); 200 is our stand-in for the upper bound and 20 for 'numerous' with no stated lower bound.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, 290: ovary of 2 to several carpels; 'several' read as up to 20 (Floral Diagrams p. 130: 2 to many).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288: hypanthium absent, rarely present; flowers hypogynous, rarely perigynous.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: poppies with 2 (or 3) sepals and twice as many petals; the bleeding-hearts (Fumariaceae) with sepals 2, small and scale-like, and petals 4 in 2 dissimilar pairs; ovary superior. Merosity 2: two sepals, and petals in two pairs.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 267 Papaveraceae (poppies) and 268 Fumariaceae (bleeding hearts and fumitories), which APG joins as Papaveraceae: annual to perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or small trees; leaves alternate (rarely the floral ones opposite), often much divided; stipules none; fruit a capsule opening by valves or pores, in the fumitories a capsule or a nut.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 267 Papaveraceae (poppies) and 268 Fumariaceae (bleeding hearts and fumitories), which APG joins as Papaveraceae: annual to perennial herbs, rarely shrubs or small trees; leaves alternate (rarely the floral ones opposite), often much divided; stipules none; fruit a capsule opening by valves or pores, in the fumitories a capsule or a nut. The books add opposite (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288: alternate (spiral) to nearly opposite.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Papaveraceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Fumariaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Papaveraceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Fumariaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Papaveraceae with Fumariaceae: flowers regular or irregular as coded, a state the authors qualify keeping its word (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Papaveraceae with Fumariaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_division.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Papaveraceae with Fumariaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple usually, compound sometimes; the simple blade dissected usually, none sometimes; lobes or leaflets pinnate usually, palmate sometimes. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta).

traits.leaf_incision.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Papaveraceae with Fumariaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves simple usually, compound sometimes; the simple blade dissected usually, none sometimes; lobes or leaflets pinnate usually, palmate sometimes. Read from the coded leaf form and dissection by script (spec-rework/b1/delta). The books add lobed (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288: lobed, divided or dissected.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Papaveraceae (read 2026-10-17): terminal flowers solitary in many, otherwise cymose or racemose inflorescences. Corydalis (~540 of ~775 spp, Wikipedia Corydalis) and Fumaria bear racemes, so raceme leads; single flowers in Papaver and Meconopsis. Raceme added as a new state. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 288, family Papaveraceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".
